title: BA1/1519/2020 of SURAJ Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 1519 of 2020
Suraj ...Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ....Opposite party
Present:
Mr. Gaurav Singh, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. T.C. Agarwal, DAG for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Applicant, Suraj, who is in judicial custody, in Case
Crime No. 265 of 2020, under Sections 363, 366A, 376 (2) (n)
IPC and Section 5 (l)/6 of Protection of Children From Sexual
Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Laksar, District Haridwar, has
sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties through video
conferencing.
3. In this case, FIR was lodged by the mother of the
victim that her daughter is missing from her house since
01.04.2020. A suspicion was raised that it is the applicant, who
had enticed her.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would argue that
the victim was in love with the applicant; applicant is 24 years
young boy and the victim had completed 17 years on 01.04.2020,
when she left her house; she left her house on her own without
any inducement; they married thereafter on 02.04.2020 in a
temple at Laksar and the victim has stated that they established
relations thereafter. It is argued that the victim is married wife of

2
the applicant and no offence has been committed. Especially,
reference has been given to Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC.
5. On behalf of the State, it is argued that there is no
proof of marriage and the girl was minor on the date of incident.
6. In fact, there is no proof as such of marriage, no
marriage certificate and no marriage photograph with the bail
application. But, the statements of the victim recorded under
Sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
are on record, in which she has categorically stated that she was
in love with the applicant and she left her house on her own on
01.04.2020 and married to applicant on 02.04.2020.
7. Having considered all the submissions, under the facts
and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that the
applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
8. The bail application is allowed.
9. Let the applicant, namely, Suraj, be released on bail, on
his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties,
each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
10. This bail order be forwarded to concerned Court as well
as the concerned jail through e-mail also.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 11.09.2020
Jitendra
